entities.summary: Nyuserre Ini was an Ancient Egyptian king, the sixth ruler of the Fifth Dynasty during the Old Kingdom period. He is credited with a reign of 24 to 36 years depending on the scholar, and likely lived in the second half of the 25th century BCE. Nyuserre was the younger son of Neferirkare Kakai and queen Khentkaus II, and the brother of the short-lived king Neferefre. He may have succeeded his brother directly, as indicated by much later historical sources. Alternatively, Shepseskare may have reigned between the two as advocated by Miroslav Verner, albeit only for a few weeks or months at the most.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a ruler of the Fifth Dynasty, Nyuserre Ini played a significant role in shaping Ancient Egyptian history during the Old Kingdom period. His reign spanned approximately 24-36 years and had regional implications for Egypt's politics and economy.
